co-production and co-management are not only possible, but also desirable, in many situations.
co-production is a complex process that is influenced by the institutional environment and that it is not always beneficial for all parties involved.

the following questions: What are the implications of co-production and the involvement of the third sector in public service delivery for the relationship between citizens and public authorities?
how and why third sector organisations are involved in public service provision, and how they are involved.
how the third sector can and does play a role in the delivery of public goods and services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the third sector is a heterogeneous and diverse group of organizations, and the role of the sector in public service provision is equally varied.
co-production is a useful concept to understand the role of the third sector in public service delivery, but it is not a magic wand that can solve all the problems of service delivery.
co-production, as a concept, is not yet fully developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

co-production is a useful concept for analysing the third sector's role in public service delivery, and that the co-production literature provides a good starting point to understand the role and impact of the third sector in the public sector, but also that it needs further development.
the third sector is a key actor in co-production, co-governance and co-management of public services.
we are in a process where the state, the market and the third sector are increasingly co-producing, co-managing and co-governing public services.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the third sector can be a useful partner in public service delivery.
the third sector is not a homogenous entity and the role that it plays in public services varies considerably across sectors and countries.

co-production, co-governance and co-management are not just buzz words but that they are real phenomena that have important implications for the delivery of public goods, the management of public organizations and the governance of society.
